metadata.description: Requirements-to-design traceability: functional requirements and acceptance criteria mapped to entities, business rules, and workflows

requirements.req_text: The system must accept string input via manual entry in the UI.

design_elements.description: Captures raw and normalized entries from U2; normalized_strings is the result after U1 processing
normalize() accepts raw_entries from U2; produces SortInput with normalized_strings

requirements.req_text: The system must accept string input via selection from a bundled word list.

design_elements.description: Owned by U2 (WordListProvider); picked words are merged with typed entries into raw_entries passed to U1

business_rules: BR-WLP-1 (Bundled Word List — Fixed and Immutable)

requirements.req_text: Input processing must normalize strings to lowercase when encountering capital letters; the system only allows lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters based on ASCII value.

design_elements.description: Step 3.2.3: lowercase ASCII capitals; pass non-ASCII unchanged
Contains the result after normalization

requirements.req_text: The system must preserve the original string forms as entered (after normalization rule applied consistently) in both input display and output.

design_elements.description: SortInput.raw_entries preserves original; SortInput.normalized_strings shows normalized form
raw_entries field preserves originals; normalized_strings field shows normalized result

requirements.req_text: The bundled word list must be included with the app (no external data source).

design_elements.description: Immutable, shipped with application

business_rules: BR-WLP-1 (Bundled Word List — Fixed and Immutable)

requirements.req_text: The system must implement bubble sort for strings.

design_elements.id: Workflow 2: Run All Three Algorithms → Bubble Sort
design_elements.description: Formal bubble sort algorithm with comparison and swap counting

test_cases: run_all([charlie, apple, bob]) → bubble_result with sorted_strings=[apple, bob, charlie]

requirements.req_text: The system must implement selection sort for strings.

design_elements.id: Workflow 2: Run All Three Algorithms → Selection Sort
design_elements.description: Formal selection sort algorithm (stable variant recommended) with counting

test_cases: run_all([charlie, apple, bob]) → selection_result with sorted_strings=[apple, bob, charlie]

requirements.req_text: The system must implement quick sort for strings.

design_elements.id: Workflow 2: Run All Three Algorithms → Quick Sort (Lomuto Partition)
design_elements.description: Formal quick sort with Lomuto partitioning and counting

test_cases: run_all([charlie, apple, bob]) → quick_result with sorted_strings=[apple, bob, charlie]
requirements.design_decision: Q6: Lomuto partition chosen for educational clarity

requirements.req_text: All three algorithms must sort strings lexicographically (ASCII/Unicode as-is, default lexicographic ordering).

design_elements.id: Workflow 2: Run All Three Algorithms → All per-algorithm workflows
design_elements.description: All use Python's default string comparison (<, >, ==) for lexicographic order

requirements.design_decision: Q5: Use Python's default Unicode lexicographic order for all strings
test_cases: sorted(['b', 'A', 'a']) should match all three algorithms' output
Mixed ASCII/non-ASCII: ['café', 'cafe', 'bag'] sorted by Unicode values

requirements.req_text: All three algorithms must run on the same input when sorting is triggered.

design_elements.description: run_all() invokes all three on the same normalized_strings

requirements.req_text: For each algorithm, the system must verify accuracy by comparing its sorted result against Python's built-in sorted() (default lexicographic, deterministic).

design_elements.description: AccuracyChecker.check() compares result against sorted(normalized_strings)
Record of pass/fail verification

business_rules: BR-AC-1 (Accuracy Check — Exact Match Against Reference)
test_cases: check(bubble_result, sort_input) → AccuracyCheck(passed=True) when sorted_strings matches

requirements.req_text: Accuracy must be reported as pass/fail for each algorithm (exact order match to reference).

design_elements.description: Boolean; true only on exact-order match

business_rules: BR-AC-1 (Accuracy Check — Exact Match Against Reference)

requirements.req_text: All three algorithms must be checked for accuracy independently.

design_elements.description: One check per algorithm; no cascade failures

requirements.req_text: The system must track step counts for each algorithm using the textbook definition: measure iterations of outer/inner loops as defined in the standard textbook form for each algorithm.

design_elements.id: Workflow 2: Run All Three Algorithms → Comparison Counting
design_elements.description: Formal definitions for bubble, selection, quick in Section 3 of functional-spec.md

business_rules: BR-SE-1 (Comparison Counting — Single Definition for All Algorithms)
requirements.design_decision: Q1: Resolved to 'total element comparisons' (primary metric) per FR4.2 requirement for direct cross-algorithm comparison

requirements.req_text: The same definition of 'total element comparisons' must be used as the primary comparable count for UI display across all three algorithms (to enable direct comparison).

design_elements.description: Total element comparisons; same definition for bubble, selection, quick
Each algorithm increments comparisons counter for every element-to-element comparison

business_rules: BR-SE-1 (Comparison Counting — Single Definition for All Algorithms)
test_cases: All counts are directly comparable in the UI

requirements.req_text: The system must also track and display swap counts separately for each algorithm (complementary to comparisons).

design_elements.description: Algorithm-specific swap count; secondary metric
Each algorithm counts swaps per its natural definition

requirements.req_text: Step/comparison counts are integers and must be displayed without truncation (no limits on classroom-sized inputs).

design_elements.description: Both are Python integers; no truncation or limits

requirements.req_text: For edge cases (single element, all equal), counts must be recorded correctly (e.g., minimal counts).

design_elements.description: Part 6 of functional-spec.md: empty input, single element, all identical

requirements.req_text: The UI must be implemented as a simple Streamlit application.

design_elements.description: Streamlit component in U2; imports U1 library

requirements.req_text: A single 'Sort' button must run all three algorithms on the same input and display all three results side-by-side.

design_elements.description: U2 calls run_all() once; receives three results
U2 receives three per sort run

requirements.req_text: For each algorithm, the UI must display: algorithm name, sorted list, comparisons count, swaps count, and accuracy (pass/fail).

design_elements.description: Provides algorithm name, sorted_strings, comparisons, swaps
Provides passed boolean

requirements.coverage: Data model supports; display is U2

requirements.req_text: The UI must show the input that was sorted.

design_elements.description: U2 displays this as the echo of sorted input

requirements.req_text: The UI must provide clear, intuitive presentation suitable for educational use.
If the input is empty (no strings entered/selected), the system must display a message 'Enter or select at least one string' and must not run sorting.

design_elements.description: normalize() produces empty normalized_strings; U2 validates before calling sort
U2 validates non-empty constraint; U1 does not

requirements.design_decision: Q2: U2 validates empty input before calling U1; renders message without invoking sorting
requirements.coverage: Supported by U1 (returns empty) and implemented in U2 (validation)

requirements.req_text: For a single string input, the system must return it correctly with appropriate step counts (minimal/zero as defined by algorithm implementation) and accuracy pass.

test_cases: Single element: sorted_strings = input, comparisons=0, swaps=0, passed=True

requirements.req_text: For inputs where all strings are identical, the system must return the same list correctly with accuracy pass.

test_cases: All identical: sorted_strings = input (in order), swaps=0, passed=True

requirements.req_text: The system must reject/ignore empty strings appropriately when processing input.

design_elements.description: Step 3.2.2: Drop empty tokens after trimming

Deployment to production (Streamlit Community Cloud) must occur automatically on merge to `main` via GitHub Actions (continuous deployment), consistent with team practice of auto-deploying to production on merge.
Sorting results must be exactly correct as verified against the reference sort.

design_elements.description: AccuracyChecker ensures exact-match verification

business_rules: BR-AC-1 (Accuracy Check — Exact Match Against Reference)

requirements.req_text: Step counting must be implemented consistently according to the chosen definitions.

design_elements.description: Formal algorithms with consistent comparison and swap counting

requirements.req_text: Tests (pytest) must achieve at least ~80% line coverage on sorting logic, following test-after methodology.
requirements.test_orientation: Part 10 of functional-spec.md lists key testable behaviors

design_decisions_applied.question: Step Count Definition (FR4.1 vs FR4.2)
design_decisions_applied.decision: Option A: Track ONLY total element comparisons (primary UI metric); same definition for all three
design_decisions_applied.rationale: Required by FR4.2's explicit requirement for 'same definition… as the primary comparable count… to enable direct comparison'

design_decisions_applied.question: Empty Input Handling
design_decisions_applied.decision: Option B: U2 validates before calling U1; U1 returns empty results if called
design_decisions_applied.rationale: Keeps U1 as pure computation layer per ADR-004

design_decisions_applied.question: Swap Counting Definition
design_decisions_applied.decision: Option A: Natural swap count per algorithm; no normalization
design_decisions_applied.rationale: Simpler; comparisons is the primary metric

design_decisions_applied.question: Duplicate String Handling
design_decisions_applied.decision: Option A: Stable sort (preserve input order of duplicates)
design_decisions_applied.rationale: Required by FR3.1 (exact match vs Python sorted(), which is stable)

design_decisions_applied.question: Lexicographic Ordering for Mixed ASCII/Non-ASCII
design_decisions_applied.decision: Option A: Default Python Unicode lexicographic order

design_decisions_applied.question: Quick Sort Partitioning Strategy
design_decisions_applied.rationale: Simpler, more predictable for educational use
